messages.text: I’ll rebuild the ACTS checkout against the updated Spack dependencies and verify the installed runtime before resuming the muon-system validation.

The preflight confirms that the Spack setup and lockfile changed. I’ll use the checkout’s prescribed build/install command and preserve its existing source edits. DD4hep and Geant4 are installed; their full source trees aren’t needed for this rebuild.

The first configure stopped on cached paths to the old dependencies, including Expat 2.8.5. I’ll save the old CMake cache and reconfigure from a fresh cache so ACTS resolves the current Spack packages.
Fresh configuration succeeded and found Expat 2.9.0 and vecmem 1.28.0. The full build is running with the existing plugins and Python bindings enabled.

The cache audit also found old ROOT and Python installation paths. Those packages’ version numbers hadn’t changed, so I’m checking their installation identities as well. The source edits are unchanged, and compilation is progressing.
The build is still progressing through ACTS Core. Once installation finishes, I’ll run the C++ tests and check ACTS, DD4hep, Geant4 and nODD imports in the refreshed Python environment.
ACTS Core and the DD4hep plugin have compiled. The build is now working through the examples and remaining targets; no compiler errors have appeared.
The build has reached the ROOT input/output components and is still running without errors. The test executables and Python bindings remain in the build.
The build has reached the Python plugin bindings, including Geant4. The existing ACTS source edits are still preserved.
The build is compiling the unit-test executables now. I’ll check the installed libraries, bindings and regenerated dependency pins before resuming the muon scan.
Compilation has passed through the geometry, magnetic-field and propagator test sources without errors. The remaining tests are still building.
The build is now compiling plugin tests, including DD4hep, Geant4 and JSON. Installation and runtime checks are still pending.
The full build and installation succeeded. I’m now checking the refreshed runtime and running the tests before returning to the muon-system work.

All 385 C++ tests passed. The Python checks passed with 28 tests and two skips for optional external nODD inputs; runtime imports and Geant4 dataset checks also passed. I’m finishing the focused propagation checks, then I’ll rebuild the muon adapter against this installation.

The rebuild is verified: all 385 C++ tests, the three focused propagation suites, and the Python/runtime checks passed. The source edits remain intact. I’m resuming PR #90 and will rebuild its muon adapter against the refreshed installation.

The curved-edge control caught a real navigation problem: the finite-portal approach missed an entry face. I’m retaining that failed control and adding a surface-audit mode that uses native ACTS roots, then checks each root against the finite chamber faces. The chamber geometry and field map will stay fixed.

The scan tooling now keeps failed tracks in the generated totals and separates “six large-face crossings” from “three paired stations.” That will let us distinguish lost coverage from unfinished field/navigation cases when assessing the reviewer’s segment requirement.

The revised audit recovers both faces in the first curved-edge fixture. We’re also testing a track initially parallel to a chamber side, because a missed side entry would make the paired-station count unreliable.

Field lookup agrees with the retained reader to about \(2\times10^{-14}\) T, and the native chamber geometry and straight-track crossings pass. The curved-track refinement checks still disagree, so the coverage scan remains gated while we correct native target handling.

The diagnostics found a separate ACTS forward-distance setting that was discarding valid targets near the surface. We’re correcting that setting and preserving native correction steps, then rerunning the strict controls.

Both curved-edge fixtures now pass at 10 nm and 1 nm targeting tolerances. The expanded controls are running: 256 distinct straight-track directions, plus curved-track checks across all momenta and charges with candidate-search and step-size comparisons.

The segment counts and track statuses now agree under step refinement. Some grazing crossings still shift by tens of micrometres, so I’m tightening integration accuracy while keeping the 10 µm comparison limit. The exhaustive check also exposed distant, unphysical supporting-plane targets; both searches will now use the same conservative finite-volume distance bound.

The expanded controls pass. Indexed and exhaustive searches agree exactly, and the largest crossing-position shift under refinement is 1.2 µm, below the unchanged 10 µm limit. I’m freezing the implementation and running the full momentum/charge scan.

The native scan completed, but I found a bookkeeping error in the output merger’s integrity check. I’ve corrected it and am rerunning the scan. The executable and passed native controls are unchanged.

The scan retained 148,960 tracks and 464,397 native boundary events, with no orphan crossings or unresolved navigation cases. The fixed layout does not provide six face proxies consistently over the full sphere: 39–44% are proven passes, and even assigning every unfinished field-mask case a pass only raises the bound to about 77–80%. I’m preparing the hit views and entrance maps.

Independent review found that a pure tangent contact could be counted as a large-face crossing. I’ve fixed the counter and added a regression test. The scan contains no tangent events, so the reported fractions are unchanged.

The hit views and entrance maps are ready. They show persistent coverage gaps from 2.65 GeV to 1 TeV, with field-mask cases marked as unfinished. All 81 repository science tests and the layout/hash checks pass; I’m freezing the evidence for the final independent review.

The ACTS rebuild is complete, including its C++ and Python checks. The final independent review has also reproduced every track’s chamber counters and all coverage bounds without a mismatch. I’m finishing the review record and publishing the PR update.

The main result is clear: the fixed layout gives six large-face crossings for 39–44% of sampled directions over 4π. Even counting every unfinished field-mask case as a success raises that to only 77–80%. PR #90 will include the hit views and entrance maps, with those unknown cases shown explicitly.

The independent review is complete, with no unresolved findings in its stated scope. It verified all 148,960 track counters and the four plots. I’m now pushing the evidence and replying to both PR #90 comments.
PR #90 is updated and the reviewer response is posted. The ACTS rebuild, muon-study controls and independent review all pass. I’m checking CI on the final pushed revision before closing out.
CI has passed the muon layout checks, the new ACTS evidence checks and the inherited field tests on the final revision. The remaining repository checks are still running.
The changed muon code has passed CI. The broader finite-module regression suite is still running; no failures have been reported so far.
The finite-module and pixel geometry suites have passed too. CI is finishing the export, strip-layout and repository-record checks.
All scientific and geometry CI suites have passed. Only the final record-validation and node-preflight checks remain.
The final record tests are still running without a reported failure. Those tests create fresh repository fixtures, so this step takes longer than the direct validators, which already passed locally.

CI found two broken relative links in the new ACTS README. I’m correcting them and rerunning the documentation checks. The scientific tests passed; this fix does not change the propagation code, data or results.

Both links are fixed. All 33 local documentation/journal tests and five node-preflight tests now pass. I’m checking that the correction leaves the reviewed scientific evidence unchanged, then pushing it for CI.

The follow-up check confirms that only the two README links and their manifest entry changed; all 85 checked scientific files are unchanged. The correction and its review record are ready for the final CI run.
The final CI job has started after waiting for a runner. The documentation checks pass locally, and the propagation code and datasets remain unchanged from the reviewed revision.
GitHub reports that the final job is still queued for a runner; it has not restarted the tests yet. The documentation fix has passed the local checks and the separate review.

ACTS is rebuilt against the updated Spack dependencies: 385 C++ tests, three integration runs and 28 Python checks passed, with two optional skips.

I continued the muon work and updated [PR #90](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/90) with ACTS propagation, hit views, coverage maps and the reviewer response.

The vacuum study shows coverage gaps: 39–44% proven coverage for six large chamber faces over 4π; optimistic upper bounds are 77–80%, including field-map unknowns.

Local checks and independent technical review pass. The final CI rerun is queued for a GitHub runner.
